It allows you to swipe left,right,etc... and access functions and features. It still have the Moto gestures that are features Google should have included from the beginning. Bought this Moto to try the android world and once I found an app that gave me the live tiles I had been used to I really like the phone. Solid phone at a solid price.. Purchased this after my beloved Moto X Pure suffered a cracked screen. Absolutely no complaints so far. Excellent MOTO!. This phone is everything I thought it would be. Great pictures, apps, speed, etc. It is well worth the money!

Lots of calls, Facebook, email, you tube, various productivity apps... etc. I can go pretty much 3 days between charges and when it needs it, the phone charges fast. Not impressed like previous Moto Gs. I bought this phone after having a Moto 3 that I liked that finally succumbed to a concrete floor after somehow surviving being buried in a snow drift for a couple weeks. The downside is that in several ways it feels like a definite step back from the Moto 3, which is disappointing. The good? Hit or miss. Read if yours have random crash or restarts. I purchased this moto G plus 5 (with Amazon ad) when it was on sale with the lightning deal. Best of the mid-range phones, a King has come!. Bought on another e-tailer site on a Black Friday deal. This is the second one I've bought, previous was purchased from a big blue box retailer. I migrated from a Samusung Galaxy S5 on the Verizon network. Pros: You're not going to get a better performer at this price point. Long battery life, snappy performance, stock android (no bloatware), and service unlocked (works well on Verizon). 64gb storage to avoid "forced obsolescence", 4gb RAM, and an EXCELLENT fingerprint reader, better than the S5 even!. Love the "Moto Actions" app that allows the home / fingerprint reader button to act as a "back" and "active apps" button as well, giving more room on screen for apps by eliminating those from the display. Most Verizon apps still work (Message+, Visual Voicemail), except "My Verizon".

What I found are, relative to the iPhone, are: it does not focus as accurately and often missed focusing on people in photos, the shutter lag is very long, it does not do well in lower light situations, it can't handle backlit scenes very well, photos were generally darker lacking detail in shadows, and takes a very long time to save panorama photos. So, if you are a photo oriented person - I would be careful with this phone.

Came from last years G4. This is a worthy successor.. After having multiple issues with the Moto G4 32gb for the past year, I finally picked up this new phone on a Amazon Prime Day special. More ram, faster cpu and a better camera (faster picture capture and better quality) . This is well worth the upgrade. It has minimal lag between apps and the Amazon ads aren't intrusive.

Primarily, the lack of speedy updates. Most Android developers seem to miss this mark, though (aside from Google itself), so it seems more of an Android thing than a Moto/Lenovo thing. It's very likely the G5+ will get at least Android O at some point, albeit a bit later than most would like. Still, it would be nice to see Lenovo follow up on their initial promises to get faster updates out. Other issues are a glitchy light sensor (seems to not always brighten up when it should), a tweaky sleep/daydream mode (I've seen it stay awake past the set timer for no reason, but this seems rather rare), and, as of August 2017, a glitchy Google app that freezes up sometimes (though this is really Google's fault, as it wasn't always this way according to reviews and others who have had the phone longer).

I don't play games on my phone so I can't say whether it's good for that, but Spotify, YouTube and various social media apps work very well. Amazon Ads are not very intrusive, and if you want you can have apps (like Weather Channel) that have persistent notifications and it keeps the ads from covering your whole screen, it essentially turns them into a notification. I can't wait to see Motorola's next G device, this one has made me a big fan.
Good quality product. Good everyday phone for the price. Its camera function is not as great as a Samsung Galaxy but it processor speed, memory and display combined to offer a good everyday phone.

Amazon App doesn't work. Can't connect to Android Wear/Wear OS watches.. Great specs for the price. Overall, I like the phone. HOWEVER, the Amazon app constantly closes and is unusable. And it's pretty annoying to have to close the notice telling me that the app closed. Maybe this is a good thing since it will limit my access to Amazon and spending more money. Battery life-stellar. Screen-great in most conditions Photos-Pretty darn good Speed-Just right Size-Great compromise of larger screen/smaller body. Later that year in June or July, I wound up getting a great deal on an iPhone 7 and a free phone line, and wound up with two phones and two lines. Good phone, happy owner. Great phone for the money. GREAT Phone for the $. This phone is just great and does everything I need it to do. I bought the 64/4G RAM option and Android seems to run much smoother. Pretty good.. Great amount of space and fast enough processor for everyday needs. Good camera but not so great incoming call volume.

Incredible Phone. Excellent Value.. This is an awesome phone. I purchased it back in May, and I have not had any issues. it is faster than my old Galaxy S5 and call volume and quality is good with AT&T. I have no way of knowing how many recharge cycles are left on it, or if a new one was installed as part of the refurb process. Great, Cheap Phone. Coming from the G3, this is a way better tool for a very decent price. Much faster (4GB internal) while remaining not too big to be handled with one hand. Outstanding phone; great price/value.. I really like this phone! The battery life is outstanding and it is blazing fast. The huge memory allows for all my apps with plenty of room for personal files. Considering this, as well as the modest price, this phone is a real winner.

I do tend to trust certified refurbs in general, because the way I see it is that if the repair person was competent, any problems have now been taken care of. Almost like a secondary quality control. The software updated several times right away after the phone was activated, bringing the security patches up to date. The Android version did not update, and I don't expect it to. The hardware is designed for a specific version of Android, and going much beyond that can cause problems. Having said that, I have seen one report that said Android Oreo seemed to have better performance on this phone. If I see many other reports in agreement with this, I may consider it.

it is faster than my old Galaxy S5 and call volume and quality is good with AT&T. My initial impression of this phone is very positive, it is faster than my old Galaxy S5 and call volume and quality is good with AT&T. I did have an issue with the Amazon Underground app crashing. The phone kept displaying a message saying "Amazon keeps stopping". The Amazon video app would also display an error when started but it would run unlike the underground app which would just crash. To fix it, I had to disable the Amazon video app so that the underground app would start. Once the underground app would start, I signed out and back in. Once I was logged back in, I re-enabled the amazon video app and it started working as well. I don't think I'll use the underground or video apps much but it was annoying to constantly get error messages. Hope this helps someone.

I'm pretty hard on my phones. I have been searching for a new phone for a while. Rather than pay $30/month or 650 out of pocket, I have been trying some of the entry level phones. most are so slow that after two months of use they're a paperweight. I'm pretty hard on my phones, using them for a lot of different things all day long. I have lots of database apps for research for my work, and use them for exercise, food tracking, multiple email accounts, lots of web browsing. I have not really tried games on it so I can't speak to that. This phone has stood up really well. I LOVE the vanilla android experience vs some bloated crap from asus or samsung. Even if the phone dies for some reason, I will gladly fork over the money to replace it with the exact same phone.

That's only if you use multiple inputs though (including Google voice typing) so it may not be an issue for most people. Even if you do use multiple keyboards, it's not a huge issue, just something small that could be polished up. Update 1/31/2018: The battery has started depleting much quicker than before. I would never go below 50% after a day of moderate usage but now I'm getting to levels around the 30% mark by the time I get home (9-5). I rarely use my phone for calling, mostly text messages and the internet. I always keep my brightness at fairly low levels (maybe 1/8 of the way). The phone is also starting to get laggy to the point of needing to be restarted much more frequently, at around once a week. Lag is especially noticeable for swipe typing.

battery life seems to be good so far though. the phone does it job for the most part. I noticed it started to slow down after only 2 months. Now it takes up to a minute to open an app if multiple are open and its speed is now of an 2 year old galaxy. battery life seems to be good so far though.

Many hardware and software malfunctions that are actively prevalent after less than a month of using the phone.. Been using this phone for about 4 months. Pros: -Speaker for media and phone calls are both located in the speaker above the screen with is much better than on the back of the device or the bottom. -Fingerprint reader has this cool feature to be used as the original android 4.0 3 button ui. Swipe left on it to use the back feature and swipe right to open app manager and tap to go to the home screen, and hold down for 3 seconds to open google assistant. RAM is 4gb and hasnt become laggy at all, still performs great. -Battery life is great.

Exceptional value for money. Everyday work hose.. Activated phone yesterday. Two things I immediately admitted: the weight of the unit and washed-out colors, the lack of red. That were more pronounced at photos, interface colors are basically fine. SIM card was recognized as soon as it was inserted without the reboot. The overall performance seems to be fine. Initial sounds are quite intrusive and need to be changed for business settings. What really was a deal breaker for me was that LGs 360 CAMERA Manager app could not connect to the camera. I spent few hours trying to make it work to no avail. The app works /connects flowlessly on Nexus 5 and Samsung 5s phones, but not on this one. I even updated firmware on the Camera , still no luck. I don't expect neither Lenovo, no LG support to land me a hand so will probably return the device.

Best of the mid-range phones, a King has come!. Bought on another e-tailer site on a Black Friday deal. This is the second one I've bought, previous was purchased from a big blue box retailer. I migrated from a Samusung Galaxy S5 on the Verizon network. Pros: You're not going to get a better performer at this price point. Long battery life, snappy performance, stock android (no bloatware), and service unlocked (works well on Verizon). 64gb storage to avoid "forced obsolescence", 4gb RAM, and an EXCELLENT fingerprint reader, better than the S5 even!. Love the "Moto Actions" app that allows the home / fingerprint reader button to act as a "back" and "active apps" button as well, giving more room on screen for apps by eliminating those from the display. Most Verizon apps still work (Message+, Visual Voicemail), except "My Verizon".

Lots of calls, Facebook, email, you tube, various productivity apps... etc. I can go pretty much 3 days between charges and when it needs it, the phone charges fast. My old Lumia needed to be charged frequently even when it was new and every night the iPhone and the Samsung Galaxy in my house are on their chargers or they are both bricks the next day. Not the Moto G Plus, but excellent batter life comes with some big tradeoffs. Processor speed. This is a harder one for me to evaluate since I was upgrading from a phone that was a couple generations old and running an antiquated OS, but this phone seems fast. I surf along with others in the family using higher end phones and don't seem to be noticeably behind and the performance well outpaces what I upgraded from. Size and dimensions.

Had an amazing battery life initially. Had an amazing battery life initially, but after installing a few apps, the phone barely makes it through the day. Installed an app to find the culprit. No luck, 90% of the time is used by , Google play service, totally opaque.
Frustrated. Crashes and restarts about 3 times day. Applications like Chrome also lag and crash. Wost phone I have ever owned.
Phone is excellent quality and works very well. Phone is excellent quality and works very well. App selection should be up to owner and not supplier. The price for phone was outstanding.

Constantly crashes with Android 8. Just continuously crashes in Gmail, Messages, Photos, YouTube, even the keyboard. All apps with user input, especially the Amazon app which I use a lot. Crashes every few minutes while trying to use apps with the touch screen. Runs ok with audio apps with screen turned off like Audible. It was more stable before the Android 8 update. Otherwise, I like the RAM and storage and CPU. Should be the best phone I've ever owned. Should be.

Outstanding phone; great price/value.. I really like this phone! The battery life is outstanding and it is blazing fast. The huge memory allows for all my apps with plenty of room for personal files. Considering this, as well as the modest price, this phone is a real winner.

Since I was using it for work the answer was always yes, I need this picture to attach to the site report, but sometimes it takes 1 or 2 tries, sometimes 10. Then they decided to start screwing with basic usability, you ever tap the Google search bar and nothing happens? You ever do that 4 or 5 times every time you want to look something up? Then the true Moto personality came out, after a few weeks of slowly degrading usability it gave me the cherry on top and EVERYTHING took 2 or 3 tries to input. Play games? Not anymore after your commands are just ignored until you die, fail, fall etc, and the Google launch glitch has hit it's final evolution, it ignores you for a few tries, then finally calls up Google search, but does not display the keyboard to enter search terms.

Good for the price but there are sacrifices. I bought this to replace my busted Nexus 5X (boot loop hell). I have the no-ads, 64/4 GB version. I've been using it for 8 weeks, at the time of this review. Likes: - Snappy performance. Chipset and RAM are more than adequate for my casual usage. No hiccups when gaming or using other apps. - Screen. Bright and colors pop. No problems with screen sensitivity. - Operating system. Pretty much a stock version of Android. It has a few little tweaks that can be turned on, or not, but no obtrusive software or bloatware. - Battery. Much better than my 5X. I can get about 2 days of battery life with casual use. Sacrifices: - No NFC chip, which means no tap-to-pay capability. I enjoyed this feature on my 5X, and really miss it here.

Primarily, the lack of speedy updates. Most Android developers seem to miss this mark, though (aside from Google itself), so it seems more of an Android thing than a Moto/Lenovo thing. It's very likely the G5+ will get at least Android O at some point, albeit a bit later than most would like. Still, it would be nice to see Lenovo follow up on their initial promises to get faster updates out. Other issues are a glitchy light sensor (seems to not always brighten up when it should), a tweaky sleep/daydream mode (I've seen it stay awake past the set timer for no reason, but this seems rather rare), and, as of August 2017, a glitchy Google app that freezes up sometimes (though this is really Google's fault, as it wasn't always this way according to reviews and others who have had the phone longer).

Does this phone match up pound for pound against the premium flagship models? No, but you don't expect a mid-range priced smartphone to be on equal footing with the newest iPhone or Galaxy device, That said, I've had this phone for a week now and have had plenty of time to put it through its paces as I'm one of those people who uses my smartphone more than I probably should. I do everything with it from streaming music, YouTube, etc. and this phone has impressed me with its strong battery life and its solid performance even with countless apps running in the background. Hardware wise, I'm not one who needs to have premium everything under the hood so for whatever this phone lacks compared to the high-end flagship models, it doesn't really bug me too much.

It's also much more convenient than remembering my iCloud password. I guess it may be considered a "big" phone, but I think it still feels sleek and only exemplifies the beautiful resolution of the screen. From the second you turn it on, and the "Hello Moto!" Animation plays... I promise you'll be impressed. I'd still pick my old MacBook over my new Windows laptop any day, but Android's operating system has really impressed me as far as speed and ease of use. Because of some security concerns, I'd recommend you download an app like Lookout to protect yourself since Android is more vunerable than iOS as a fact. You can choose to turn off the Amazon alerts and apps if you'd like, so there's no reason not to choose the cheaper option.
The owner is very happy with the phone. I bought the phone as a gift. The owner is very happy with the phone.

This is *almost* my favorite phone ever, but the shortcomings are painful.. * I'm reviewing the unlocked amazon prime exclusive 64mb Moto g5 plus (USA version) on Sprint + The migration from an iPhone 7 was straightforward. I have my contacts, photos and music. Migrating photos was time-consuming but not overly onerous. + The price ($219) was a great value + The phone works on Sprint's network except Sprint's visual voicemail app is not available. I'm using YouMail's app which very well may be superior. I tried two Sprint stores before finding one with the required SIM in stock. + Unlike iMessage, Android's messaging app works well when roaming in weak coverage without LTE + The fingerprint sensor is *far* superior to the iPhone 7 + Radio performance when roaming in weak signal areas is comparable to iPhone 7 + Camera is comparable to iPhone 7.

It also randomly opens apps in the background. I have a lot of apps and many of them crash regularly. If you are looking for an affordable phone as a backup or maybe for your teenager, this is a good choice. But if you use your phone as more than just a phone (i.e. you run lots of apps, stream movies and music, use navigation, want more assistant type capabilities, etc.) you might want to look elsewhere.

Great, Cheap Phone. Coming from the G3, this is a way better tool for a very decent price. Much faster (4GB internal) while remaining not too big to be handled with one hand. I love the Home/Sensor button you can program to play the roles of the regular 3 Android selectors (Back, Home, Apps). I bought the cheaper version with the Ads but barely notice them while unlocking. Not a big deal - I actually like it, it gives me gift ideas. The screen definition is great and the camera is OK (better in daylight). It took me some brain power to figure out how the SIM and SD cards all fit in the receptacle. Overall, great buy for my regular usage.

Great mobile android computer - average or below phone.... Phone is quick and responsive. Would give it top ratings for data, browsing, games etc. Unfortunately, I actually use my phone to talk with people. And it drops calls FREQUENTLY. Great mobile android computer - average or below phone...

Good deal.. Awesome device for the money... Unfortunately I never found out (and still... ) which is the proper or recommended sd card to use as internal memory. Even if the phone is 64GB/4GB version it lags from time, with mid-multitasking. Amazon apps are not as well integrated as in Amazon devices.

It is taking some time getting used but so far I love it. The ads do not bother me at .... This is the first Android I've owned. I have always had an I phone. It is taking some time getting used but so far I love it. The ads do not bother me at all.They actually have some deals on Amazon. I think I'm done with apple and there outrageous prices.

The only thing that got screwed up, both the earpiece speaker and microphone are a bit too directional. They are prone to not handling the audio properly if not well aligned with your ear or mouth. The mic port is easily blocked as well.

These lower cost phones are notorious for not being upgraded to the latest version of Android. The G5 Plus may suffer from this as well. Lenovo hasn't been upgrading many of the Moto phones - and even the G5 Plus is at 7.0 - with the latest release being 7.1.2 With all that being said - as a stand alone device - working on WiFi it has exceeded all my expectations for a $239 phone. RAM usage is around 2G of the 4G available. The phone is snappy. All the Google Apps work well on it. Hangouts video calling as well as Google Voice calling work quite well on WiFi. One potential annoyance - is you have to scan your fingerprint twice to unlock. From what I read is this is so you see the Amazon ads - but I'm not sure.

Hit or miss. Read if yours have random crash or restarts. I purchased this moto G plus 5 (with Amazon ad) when it was on sale with the lightning deal. It was straight forward to migrate from an iPhone 6 and I was up and running after some setup. The phone was snappy. No issues whatsoever. The only cons I saw were the camera (slow and delayed) and smaller screen size(I prefer a bigger screen than what it is). But hey, for what I paid , it is a very capable and adequate phone. Unfortunately, after few days of use, I started seeing Random crashes or restarts. The frequency of restarts was tolerable maybe once every other day. I noticed the restarts were getting more frequent and annoying and was debating what to do. Googled around and found this to be a common problem.

Best Battery life of any phone I've had. But very poor in almost every other category. I've had to factory reboot multiple times. Huge inconvenience every time. First two times were due to every app crashing whenever I opened one. No explanation or reason why when I called tech support. One time my phone refused to turn on for an entire day. Another time the phone randomly deleted all my texts and call history. And now the phone is unbearably slow no matter what I do, I've used used multiple task killer apps and Clean Masters. The text messaging application crashes constantly along with other messaging apps, despite multiple reinstallations. Camera picture quality is very poor. Group Messaging is very poor as well, usually lose 1/6 incoming texts, on top of arriving out of order, in many cases I have to manually download each text. The ONLY redeeming factor is the battery life which is very good. In my opinion, just not worth the frustration.

I use them often. I also use it for boat navigation, and so opening on the touch of my thumb is a very important feature when I have to access my phone quickly to adjust navigation. The battery life is great, and I end most days above 50%. it also will run navigation on GPS without inordinately depleting the battery. It has also performed decently well in the cold. When my daughter's iPhone precipitously died, my phone seem to be holding its battery strength very well.
Love It.. Works great. Have had almost no problems. Can run multiple apps at once and no crashing and tons of speed.

Amazon App doesn't work. Can't connect to Android Wear/Wear OS watches.. Great specs for the price. Overall, I like the phone. HOWEVER, the Amazon app constantly closes and is unusable. And it's pretty annoying to have to close the notice telling me that the app closed. Maybe this is a good thing since it will limit my access to Amazon and spending more money. Also, I cannot get bluetooth to connect to either my Moto 360 or my Wear 24. The phone will connect with another Moto G5 via bluetooth but I have also tried other bluetooth devices (headphones, keyboard, mouse) and they will not connect either. Battery life seems great. Really like the display but the auto-brightness doesn't seem to work all of the time. Apps seem to load quickly. App updates through the Play Store seem really fast. I love the fingerprint "button" and all it can do.

Not impressed like previous Moto Gs. I bought this phone after having a Moto 3 that I liked that finally succumbed to a concrete floor after somehow surviving being buried in a snow drift for a couple weeks. The short of it is that it is (slightly) bigger and better in terms of specs and being able to run apps. The downside is that in several ways it feels like a definite step back from the Moto 3, which is disappointing. The good? Well, it's obviously faster than my old phone and I haven't found much it can't do with ease although I'm not much of a power user (snapchat still lugs and crashes, but I think that's the app's problem). The display is crisp with good colors. It has a fingerprint scanner that works well for unlocking. It's reasonably light and it looks good without a case with a nice brushed aluminum finish.

Phone runs apps like molasis in winter.. This looked like a good phone at a reasonable price. It worked well for the first few days; there was some getting used to it which I'd expect from any new phone. The problem that I have with it now is that it has suddenly started to run EXTREMELY SLOW. It can take up to a minute to open some apps. The screen doesn't give me any kind of icon to answer new inbound calls which often results in missed calls, even texting now will fail and give an error message. Frequently I will get the message the app is not responding; do you want to close it, wait for it, or send a report. It's crazy slow when it gets into this mode. I hate to think that I am going to have to put up with this for the next couple years.
Great phone. Everything I expected from mid range phone. It is great for doing the everyday things.
Not the best. It's an ok phone. It's a bit laggy though. Startup takes about 5 minutes. Apps crash constantly.

If I listen to Amazon Music for 5 hours, watch a video or two, and do some light browsing, I am at 72%. This is with no adjustment or other battery saving devices or software. On an average day of about 1 and a half hours of actual use time, I am usually at around 70% and around 50% by bed time. I charge for about 30 minutes to an hour and am usually around 90%. So far, it is superior to my S5, which had a fantastic battery life. This is my best experience with any smart phone or tablet with a battery. We shall see if it lasts. I have not overcharged the phone one time so far. The biggest thing for some is the screen. The size is decent. It is rated at 5.2 inches.

No instructions, no owner's manual came w this phone.. It arrived yesterday without any instructions. If I can't get owner's manual and instructions within 4 minutes I will return it for a refund, and change my rating to 1 star. Unsatisfied now, it's up to vendor to make me a happy customer.

Everything I could want in a smartphone. This is my first smartphone, and I'm extremely happy with it. I love the gesture control for opening the flashlight and camera, as well as the fact that the fingerprint scanner can also be used in place of the Back and Recent Apps buttons. The camera takes excellent pictures, and apps work quickly, without lag or stuttering. The screen size is ideal for me, and the phone fits my hand nicely. Without a case, it is a little slippery because of the aluminum back, but my case solves that issue without adding a lot of thickness. I've used my family's iPhones, but I prefer this one.

The color reproduction is not natural, 12 MP is below average if you crop or zoom photos , no laser phase detection, camera app is very plain and lacks easy controls, cannot handle bright lights . Moto X Pure is way better in camera over g5 plus. Next, having used a quad HD screen, there is noticeable difference going back to HD screen. Some of the important pros though are great speed, no heating, Android 7.0 optimization, very good battery life (easily lasts one full day 16-18 hrs of heavy usage) although battery is just 3000 mAh and quick fingerprint sensor. Overall a good device if you are not buying it for camera.
Incompatible with Verizon. According to Verizon, this phone isn't compatible with them. I have done an exchange for a new phone and we will see if that works.

All day battery. I've had this phone for 6+ months with no issues. It has wonderful battery life and lack of bloatware is refreshing. My only slight would be that the phone runs slow at time with multiple high ram uasage apps open simultaneously. I would recommend to anyone looking for a good quality phone for a value price.

This Phone Is a Plus. I love this phone. I run it on Verizon and find it much faster than the S-4 it replaced. To get a better opinion of prerformance, I asked my son to evaluate it relative to his S-6. He prefers his S-6 but thought it was fast and well-designed. I received it quickly through Prime and the activation was a matter of a sim card and transferring data via an app. Good experience.

On prior devices I've used (Samsung, HTC, Nexus, OnePlus), I've always used long press on the power button to enter airplane mode or reboot or power off. Initial Setup: Supplied two credentials--one for the gmail account and another for Amazon. Chose to sync up to backed up apps and settings and, within minutes, all the apps that I had on previous devices were reinstalled. All Google related app settings got restored fully as well, including things like Chrome favorites, music library, Google Drive contents, Photos albums and pictures, etc, etc. APPS: Very light on pre-installed apps. Besides the aforementioned Amazon apps, the following two are notable--the Moto app and the Device Help app. Since this is my first time on a Motorola Android device, both are proving to be quite helpful in helping me understand device specific features. Amazon Prime Exclusive Info: 1. The lock screen does show Amazon ads.

Came from last years G4. This is a worthy successor.. After having multiple issues with the Moto G4 32gb for the past year, I finally picked up this new phone on a Amazon Prime Day special. More ram, faster cpu and a better camera (faster picture capture and better quality) . This is well worth the upgrade. It has minimal lag between apps and the Amazon ads aren't intrusive.
This phone works well but crashes some apps

Restarts constantly. The phone worked fine up until the past few days. It's your basic smartphone, nothing over the top great but the price is right. Well, you get what you pay for. Lately the phone will become very glitchy and slow, with the screen and apps freezing constantly. The glitchiness escalates until the phone restarts itself. This would be fine every once in a while but it's been almost every twelve hours. It's ridiculous that this is happening only five months after receiving it.

I'll assume I got a bad one. Apps crash all the time. Gorilla Glass? It lasted 6 weeks. Every other phone has lasted at least 6 months. Basically, I'll assume I got a bad one. Apps crash all the time, so I'll have to do a reset eventually. My Samsung S5 Sport was much more user friendly, robust, reliable. This was a great price, and the memory and cpu are quite fast. But the screen breaking (with a Zeesa screen protector on it). The phone fell out of my pocket and the edge near the power switch hit a counter top. It fell less than 2 feet. I'm going to save up and get an officially 'unbreakable' screen. We'll see how long that lasts.

GREAT Phone for the $. This phone is just great and does everything I need it to do. I bought the 64/4G RAM option and Android seems to run much smoother. All apps run really quick and everything is super snappy. It also doesn’t seem to get as hot when the processor is chugging. I upgraded from the 4th Gen and its pretty much identical except Power and Volume buttons on the side are swapped (power is on the bottom now) and the audio jack moved from the top to the bottom next to the micro USB port. Also the screen size was reduced from 5.5 to 5.2 inches which makes it a little easier to handle without really noticing much of a viewing difference. Different strokes and all that but I just don’t understand spending $700+ for a mobile device when this one is available for $300.

Get the 4 GB of RAM version and you will be much happier with the performance. This is a nice budget phone. I didn't care for the Amazon adds so paid the extra $45 later to have them removed. My wife has the same phone but with 4 GB of RAM. I wish I had bought that one. It runs much smoother with less lag. This one has 2 gb of RAM and runs fine if you have 1 or 2 apps open but if you install a lot of apps and try to multitask the 2 GB of RAM do not keep up well. If you can afford another $50 do yourself a favor and get the 4 MB / 64 GB version.

Some pros and cons Pros: great battery life. I get around 6-7 hours of screen on time and it lasts me all day Light and fits great in my hands (average size) Fast and clear camera, easy to use Activated easy on Sprint CDMA network Great and simple stock UI and it runs buttery smooth Home button|finger scanner is great and I love the gestures Cons: Light sensor, phone has "adaptive brightness" which didn't adjust screen brightness as well as auto brightness No silent mode from what I can tell, just vibrate

Except for NFC good replacement for Nexus 5x. Have owned it for a couple of weeks and really like it. Having enough memory to put all the apps I want is great and adding an SD card for pictures works well. The only missing feature for me is NFC and I can live without Google pay. Works great on the T-Mobile network for me.

Not great. It's fine. I've used Samsung Galaxies for years and have been spoiled. The biggest issue for me was how incredibly slowly the phone operates. I have plenty of space left if storage, but it functions so slowly; apps freeze up or close. It's pretty frustrating.
For that price... Best option.. Awesome phone, quick and very responsive. Prev galaxy S6 owner and the only thing I wish the MOTO had was a bigger screen.
Not bad.... This seems to perform well in terms speedy and user friendly. After month of purchase, started having issues with phone i.e. camera crash, apps crash ... etc. Phone wasn't stable enough.

The selection of apps is almost so robust it is overwhelming; one criticism of most of the apps (and I guess this is not really a criticism of the OS but rather of the app writers/providers) is the fact that most apps don't seem to offer ad-less versions you could buy for a price. Some of the apps are very frustrating with how many apps they throw at you (and some ads seem to require you to get to the "kill the app" panel, not sure else what to call it, to stop the app and restart it to avoid sitting through an extended ad. So basically the hardware in light of the price would deserve 5 starts, but the annoying ad-filled apps pull the phone down to 4 stars. Still a great phone for the price.

Excellent phone. I switched from a Samsung Galaxy S6 edge. I have to say after a week or so I'm impressed. This phone handles everything I do with ease. I am not a gamer but do a lot of Amazon shopping, internet browsing, and read different news sites. The camera is better than I expected and the phone speed is very good. Overall I am happy with my purchase and will probably never go back to one of the overpriced lease phones!

... do much of anything regarding graphics such as games like Pokemon GO or Hearthstone. Dceent phone for an average user BUT struggles to do much of anything regarding graphics such as games like Pokemon GO or Hearthstone. Missing NFC.

CONs: it is, despite its features, still an Android phone - which means occasionally I will hit or do something without any idea of what exactly I did and I'll have to search the internet to find how to undo it; while there are lots of apps and most are free, many of them are very ad-laden (really, an ad after EVERY play in Words with Friends?), who knows if I'll ever have the option of installing the next version of Android; sound is rather thin (admittedly, just about every phone I've heard playing music suffers from this but my Windows phone struck me as having somewhat better sound).

After Android 8.1 update WiFi is non functional. The phone was fine and I really liked it until it updated to Android 8.1. Now the WiFi doesn't work for most of the apps in my phone: Amazon, Netflix, Twitter, and more. I am forced to use data on the majority of my apps. I've tried every troubleshooting the "genuises" at Google gave me, nothing worked. It has been frustrating and I don't want this phone anymore, not if it can't handle an update and offer actual functionality.

I miss my normal gallery app. It has the Google app as a screen to the left of your first home screen. I don't use Google for anything. So I don't need it there constantly being expanded. The wide screen is nice. The tray was hard 2 work. My sim kept popping up. It was hard to put the memory card in the back without the sim falling out. i would've rathered there been a pop out opening for the memory like back in the day. It charges very quickly. But it also burns up fast if used lightly. Just checking bank app and deleting photos after 5 hours on 70%. I've never seen a phone this big lose power so fast. No music, not playing videos, just updating settings.

The only other complaint besides call quality I can think of is that the phone seems to be incapable of remembering an app's state for very long. Sometimes I'll open an article to read, then switch over to another app for a bit, then switch back to the article but it will disappear and reset the app to the landing page, this is a really minor but annoying gripe.

Battery life-stellar. Screen-great in most conditions Photos-Pretty darn good Speed-Just right Size-Great compromise of larger screen/smaller body. Later that year in June or July, I wound up getting a great deal on an iPhone 7 and a free phone line, and wound up with two phones and two lines. I used the iPhone 7 as my main phone and the G5 Plus got shelved. Come November I started a delivery job that I needed a phone for as it was app based. Since I had my G5 Plus just lying about, I figured use that instead of the iPhone (plus it's paid for, iPhone isn't). That is when my love for this phone kicked into overdrive. I now use this phone daily. The app I use (Amazon Flex) is very intensive, especially on the battery.

Feel - holds sturdy and speak about the tank like design.Heavier than most of the phones due to the metal build, but after a week you will get used to it. Speed - the device has enormous RAM around 4GB for the mid range processor, It handles most tasks easily like HDR processing, switching apps, 4k video recording and so on as it is the best 2017 processor. the process is a Qualcomm MSM8953 Snapdragon 625 Adreno 506 4GB RAM Battery - Battery retention is based on 2 criteria's what is the processor used and the type of battery used. it uses 3000 mAh LI-Ion which is way better than some of the LG and Chinese brands uses Li-PO. On top of it the processor gives the support to the processor to utilize the battery wisely as 600 series processors tend to be less power hungry than the 800 series.
